title: Roman Crosswalks
sentences: Pompeii's streets had stepping stones, and they tell us something about the traffic.
Big stones stood in the road so walkers could cross without stepping down.
Curbs were high, on average over thirty centimeters.
Researchers count more than three hundred crossing stones, far more than in any other known Roman city.
Carts had to straddle them, and wheels wore deep ruts into the paving.
Wear marks suggest many narrow streets were one way.
